narration.transcript: Want the look of old timber beams without the weight? Meet Heritage Timber by Ekena Millwork. Each beam is cast from real, weathered timber, so it looks solid, even up close. A five and a half inch beam, twelve feet long, ships at about eighteen pounds. One person can lift it. It slides over a wood block with standard household tools, and it's hollow so it can hide wiring. And unlike solid wood, it resists warping and cracking with less upkeep. Pick from six hand-stained finishes, or primed, eight cross-section sizes in lengths from four to twenty-four feet. It's in stock and usually ships in three to five business days. Order a sample and see it in your own light.

findings.what: In 16:9 the Smokey Brown swatch inset (about x 775–1145, y 195–560) is drawn under the spec table. The table covers roughly its right quarter, so the only image of the finish is partly hidden behind text for the whole time it shows.
findings.fix: render/videos/heritage-hero.mjs, 'choose' timeline key (Smokey Brown beat): move the inset clear of the spec table, e.g. to the left side above the finish label, or hold the table back until the inset has gone. One shared cause with the 9:16 finding: the inset is positioned without checking the spec-table and finish-panel boxes.

findings.what: In 9:16 the Smokey Brown swatch inset runs down behind the dark finish panel. The panel and the 'Smokey Brown' name cover the bottom of the swatch (about y 790–920 of 1920), so the swatch's lower edge is cut off by text.
findings.fix: render/videos/heritage-hero.mjs, 'choose' key, 9:16 layout: shrink the inset or raise it so its bottom sits above the finish panel (panel top ≈ y 790), with a gap.

findings.what: While the label reads 'HAND-STAINED · SWATCH / Smokey Brown', the room behind it is still the Natural White Oak render (BMSTWO-07). The ceiling beams, which take up most of the frame, are light tan, not Smokey Brown's grey-brown. Every other finish shows its own room, so viewers read these beams as Smokey Brown.
findings.fix: render/videos/heritage-hero.mjs, 'choose' key: for the Smokey Brown beat, take the room out (heavy dim/blur, or a plain panel) so only Ekena's swatch carries the finish. Or use Ekena's Smokey Brown beam shot (heritage__room-renders__BMSTSB-05.jpg) full panel. Don't leave another finish's beams under the label.

findings.what: In 9:16, after the kitchen was lightened, the white '24–72' (f≈2812–2880) sits on the white herringbone backsplash and range hood, so the digits break up. 'hours' (pale green) is on the bright counter and can barely be read, which leaves the primed lead-time claim without its unit. '3–5' runs across the underside of the front beam.
findings.fix: render/videos/heritage-hero.mjs, 'ship' key, 9:16 layout: put the two stats on a dark panel (like the 9:16 finish panel in 'choose', 78% #141818), or keep the lighter grade overall but add a local shade behind the stat block (y ≈ 0.38–0.72). Keep the stats off the beam.

findings.what: The narrator says 'eighteen' at f1007–1028 (Whisper word times on the delivered audio), but the counter is still at 6–16 lb then. It lands on 18 at f1037, during 'pounds', about 0.5 s after the word starts. The re-narration moved the word earlier; v7 landed on it.
findings.fix: render/videos/heritage-hero.mjs, 'weight' key, weight_18 count-up: end the count at f1007–1011 (start it about 15 frames earlier, or shorten it) so 18 lands on 'eighteen'.
